correctness.rationale: Exact one-round inclusion–exclusion followed by independent temporal products gives the covariance and time-independent sign. Strict monotonicity of the pair-inclusion probability in union overlap proves a single transition, including boundary cases. Omission duality proves the r=n-1 identity. A uniform falling-factorial log expansion, integral mean-value identity and hypergeometric-to-Poisson factorial moments give the proportional-block square-root transition, time-scaled covariance and global sign census. All proof hypotheses are explicit, and bundled exact enumeration/numerical checks passed 2,870 assertions.

value.rationale: The sign of pairwise noncoverage dependence is structurally relevant to second-moment and Poisson analyses of random covering designs. The natural square-root regime is where independent target intersections become nondegenerate and finite-population sampling competes with shared overlap. The phase theorem gives a complete all-parameter sign ordering and an asymptotic global fraction of negative covariance pairs; in a natural example most intersecting target pairs are negatively correlated. This is a motivated dependence phenomenon rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a repeated cover-time estimate.
